subject.title: fix(msteams): add timeouts to file consent upload requests

question: Which PR should establish the canonical Microsoft Teams upload-timeout helper and transfer policy before the other branch rebases onto it?
rationale: Both open PRs independently modify the same timeout owner and make the same compatibility-sensitive choice about when an existing upload must fail, so contributor-side code changes cannot safely select the permanent policy or landing order.

options.title: Land consent timeout first
options.body: Approve this narrower file-consent implementation, merge it as the canonical helper owner, then require the broader SharePoint PR to rebase and reuse it.

options.title: Land SharePoint timeout first
options.body: Approve and merge the broader SharePoint PR first, then rebase this PR so it only adds the file-consent wiring and focused tests.

options.title: Consolidate both branches
options.body: Pause both PRs and ask for one coordinated Microsoft Teams timeout PR covering consent and SharePoint delivery paths together.

recommendation.title: Land consent timeout first
recommendation.body: Approve this narrower file-consent implementation, merge it as the canonical helper owner, then require the broader SharePoint PR to rebase and reuse it.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior focused file-consent security commit makes this person the strongest available owner for the shared delivery-policy decision.
